t: LeetCode 3265 – Count Almost Equal Pairs I
o: Two numbers are almost equal if one single digit swap (in either number, leading zeros allowed) can make them equal. With n ≤ 100, generate for each number the set of values reachable by swapping any two digits (plus the number itself) and test membership pairwise. Note the trap from example 3: 123 and 231 share the same digit multiset but are NOT almost equal, so bucketing by sorted digits alone overcounts — it is only a safe pre-filter.
k: Reachable set of x = {x} ∪ {swap two digits of x}; pairs are found by set membership.
Sorted-digit signatures are a filter, not a proof — always verify with the swap set.

a.i: Precompute variants(x) for every number (identity plus all C(d,2) digit transpositions, parsed back as int so leading zeros vanish naturally). Pair (i, j) counts iff nums[j] ∈ variants(nums[i]).
s: For each number build its variant set.
Double loop over i < j; count when nums[j] is in variants[i].
a.t: O(n² + n·d²) with d ≤ 7 digits — trivial at n ≤ 100

a.n: Approach 2: Bucket by digit multiset, verify inside buckets
a.i: Numbers can only be almost equal if they share the same multiset of digits (after stripping leading zeros of swapped results — parse-as-int handles that). Group by the sorted digit signature, then run the exact variant-set test only within each group, cutting the pairwise work substantially when duplicates cluster.
s: Key each number by its sorted digits.
Within each bucket, pairwise-test with variant sets as in Approach 1.
a.t: O(n·d² + Σ bucket² · lookup) — usually much less than the raw double loop

w: At n ≤ 100 the plain double loop is the right interview answer; mention the bucketing optimization for the n = 3·10^5 sequel. Pitfalls: forgetting the identity variant (equal numbers are almost equal — example 2's five 1s give 10 pairs), and assuming equal digit multisets suffice (example 3 disproves it). Leading zeros: converting back to int discards them, matching the problem's allowance. Follow-up: the Large version demands signature-based counting with careful tie handling.
